A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PATHs study and contain complete main text, figures, tables, and appendices. Full-text comparison and page rendering support reliable comparison, including the appendix prompts and examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original analyses of Bing Copilot and WildChat conversations, including behavioral frequencies, PCA results, intent–behavior regressions, classifier validation, and qualitative findings.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical analyses and their results, including the validation tables and supplementary analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o classifiers, scalable E5/logistic task classifier, tf-idf/PCA procedure, and intent–PATH regressions are unchanged. Sections 3–4 and Appendices B–C describe the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions analyze the same English writing coverage: approximately 250,000 Bing Copilot and 68,000 WildChat sessions, with unchanged collection periods and writing categories. No dataset, population, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: No comparison method is added, removed, or revised. The classifier validations and regression-fit comparisons remain unchanged, including Appendix C.2's reference to 50% random-classifier accuracy.

E3.justification: Filtering, sampling, validation sample sizes, PCA retention criteria, regression thresholds, and qualitative-review procedures are unchanged in Appendices B–C. No existing setting is revised or new evaluation protocol introduced.

E4.justification: The behavioral case analyses in Section 6 and Appendix D are retained unchanged. Figures 13–14 report the same supplementary similarity analyses; no ablation, robustness test, or substantive case analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The regression plots retain the same significance markings and error bars, and Tables 6 and 8 retain the same Cohen's kappa reporting. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-estimation information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged, including seven PATHs explaining 80–85% of variance and the accuracies in Tables 6–8. Figure 1's substitution of shoes for knives changes illustrative wording without changing a reported finding.

T1.justification: The tf-idf representation, PCA definitions, and logistic-regression formulation in Appendix C are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: identifying recurring collaboration behaviors, relating them to writing intents, and drawing implications for LLM alignment. Their novelty claims and scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning brainstorming, learning, personalization, and session-level alignment are unchanged. Section 8 retains the same limitations concerning English-only data, unordered follow-ups, linear PCA, qualitative analysis, and privacy and safety.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C and Prompts 1–3 retain the same filtering instructions, model and software details, thresholds, and classifier prompts. Data-access information is unchanged; the added author contact details do not introduce technical or reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and the reference list are unchanged. No cited work or substantive positioning relative to earlier research is added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 adds corresponding-author markers and email addresses and makes a few punctuation edits, including the implications label in Section 6.1 and discussion headings in Section 7. The narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes 'handmade knives' to 'handmade shoes' while retaining its diagram and caption. The correspondence block slightly changes the title-page layout; the other figures and tables retain their content and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 adds author contact information, adjusts punctuation, and changes one product word in Figure 1. The methods, evidence, interpretations, limitations, and appendix material are unchanged. These small editorial edits do not meaningfully improve or weaken the paper's overall quality.
